evidence: All parse/well-formedness checks were measured locally on the frozen bytes (Python 3.12.10 tomllib, GNU bash -n, Node v24.19.0 --check, run in memory with -I -B so no cache was written). (1) TOML: task.toml, tests/scoring.toml and all five tests/*/*/judge.toml load without error. task.toml has name 'turing/hireops-recruiting-operations', schema_version 1.4, artifacts ['/app','/assets'], and the [verifier.env]/[verifier.environment] block matches the template field for field. scoring.toml is byte-identical to the template (gates render/constraints 0.0; weights 0.6/0.2/0.2; floor functional 0.05). Every judge.toml has [judge] judge='claude-code', a mode, a timeout, isolated=false and prompt_template='prompt.md'. None has model/reasoning_effort/temperature/weight. Every criterion id is unique, and every name matches RewardKit's _SAFE_NAME_RE ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ (models.py:75). Weights are positive, and the criteria have no unknown keys. Gates are binary with all_pass. Functional has 12 binary criteria, weighted_mean, weights summing to 61, which matches the comment at functional/judge.toml:23. Polish has 5 binary criteria; visual has 5 likert criteria with points=5. The MCP servers are stdio with a command, and only functional declares 'verifier' with '$APP_RESTART_HELPER'. Functional uses mode='individual'. That deviates from the batched template but is a valid JudgeMode Literal['batched','individual'] in RewardKit 0.1.7 (models.py:142), and the aggregations are in the Aggregation literal (models.py:10-12). All five prompt.md files contain {criteria} and {app_context}, which runner.py requires for prompt_template. (2) Shell: tests/test.sh and solution/solve.sh are the only *.sh files. Both start '#!/bin/bash', and 'bash -n' returns rc=0 for each. grep -rlI $'\r' over the whole frozen task finds no file with CR, so line endings are LF everywhere. tests/test.sh, Dockerfile, tools/score.py, tools/restart_mcp.py and .dockerignore are byte-identical to the template (cmp). ast.parse succeeds on score.py and restart_mcp.py. (3) Reference entry and seed: solution/app/server.js is 'require("./src/index.js")'. node --check passes for server.js, src/{bootstrap,db,index}.js and public/js/{board,threads,app}.js. The only relative requires are ./src/index.js, ./bootstrap and ./db, and all exist. index.html loads only /js/board.js, /js/threads.js and /js/app.js, which all exist. The modules deleted in the working tree (change-sets.js, rules.js, hireops.js) are not referenced. package.json, environment/assets/seed_data.json and solution/app/src/seed_data.json parse as JSON, and the two seeds are identical (sha256 a1c65c80...3740). The app honours PORT/DB_PATH (bootstrap.js:43, db.js:9) and serves /api/health (index.js:24, bootstrap.js:20), as test.sh probes at lines 48 and 136. (4) Actual run: the raw-evidence-index entries re-hash correctly, and their matching_source_files equal the frozen solution bytes, including solve.sh. via-solve.log shows the frozen solve.sh installing 11 files into an empty /app. It then shows the app running as uid 65534 with a cleared env and a real restart, with 26/26 scripted groups PASS, page_errors [], and server.log reporting '[hireops] listening on 3000' twice. (5) Budgets nest even in worst-case serial individual mode: test.sh runs rewardkit with --max-concurrent-agent 1 and budgets gates 1500 / scored 11100. That gives 12x700 + 900 + 900 = 10200 < 11100, 600+600 < 1500, and 1500+11100 < 13200. Colderwater lessons bearing on this row: lesson 10, the 128 KB prompt limit, is met. The largest single assembled functional prompt is about 8.6 KB of prompt plus 1.9 KB of app_context plus one criterion (the whole functional judge.toml is 25 KB), so well under 128 KB. Lesson 18/19, the golden harness rerun after a change, is met because the evidence is hash-bound to the current solution bytes. Lesson 11, judge infra crashes, cannot be assessed because no configured judge run exists. Counterexamples tried: (a) A broken-task-file variant, such as a duplicated TOML table key, a CRLF test.sh, or a criterion name with spaces, would be caught by the checks above, and none is present. (b) A conforming model app with ESM, another file layout or its own scripts is unaffected, because the gating files only require /app/server.js to start with node. Risk is true only because of required runtime evidence that is missing. The index scope says 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' So the frozen test.sh has not been run end to end in the built verifier image: RewardKit loading these judge.toml files from the pip harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7 install, and the MCP server startup. Acceptance was checked statically only, against a local copy of the 0.1.7 source. No parse defect was found.
